html:
The Oromo are a Cushitic-speaking people of the Horn of Africa, today the largest ethnic group in Ethiopia. The map shows their lands in the south and centre of the Ethiopian highlands from 1530 to 1800, the years when they spread across the region.

They were cattle herders and farmers governed by the Gadaa system, in which men moved through age grades every eight years, and each grade in turn held power and elected its leaders.

In the 1500s, after the long war between the Ethiopian Empire and the Adal Sultanate had worn both sides down, the Oromo moved north and east in the Oromo migrations. Within a century they had settled huge areas of the highlands and the plains around Harar.

In time many took up farming, Christianity or Islam, and some formed kingdoms, such as the Gibe states in the south-west. Oromo lords from the Yejju dynasty held real power at the Ethiopian court in the late 1700s and early 1800s. In the late 1800s Menelik II conquered the remaining independent Oromo lands and brought them into his empire.
